title: GukiZ and Binary Operations
statementMd:
We all know that GukiZ often plays with arrays.

Now he is thinking about this problem: how many arrays $*a*$, of length $*n*$, with non-negative elements **strictly less** then $2^{*l*}$ meet the following condition: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/02bd933699313baffa5788fedb6b21a78354f37e.png)? Here operation ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/625ed07379e4df241affcda9308db4df81849a5f.png) means bitwise AND (in `Pascal` it is equivalent to `and`, in `C/C++/Java/Python` it is equivalent to `&`), operation ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d8e629dfc5d72ed17b4f7da6266cd97331093ddf.png) means bitwise OR (in `Pascal` it is equivalent to ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d8e629dfc5d72ed17b4f7da6266cd97331093ddf.png), in `C/C++/Java/Python` it is equivalent to `|`).

Because the answer can be quite large, calculate it modulo $*m*$. This time GukiZ hasn't come up with solution, and needs you to help him!

## Input

First and the only line of input contains four integers $*n*$, $*k*$, $*l*$, $*m*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{18}$, $0 ≤ *k* ≤ 10^{18}$, $0 ≤ *l* ≤ 64$, $1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9} + 7$).

## Output

In the single line print the number of arrays satisfying the condition above modulo $*m*$.

## Note

In the first sample, satisfying arrays are ${1, 1}, {3, 1}, {1, 3}$.

In the second sample, only satisfying array is ${1, 1}$.

In the third sample, satisfying arrays are ${0, 3, 3}, {1, 3, 2}, {1, 3, 3}, {2, 3, 1}, {2, 3, 3}, {3, 3, 0}, {3, 3, 1}, {3, 3, 2}, {3, 3, 3}$.
